title: Immutable audit lifecycle policy enforcer
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement an enforceable lifecycle enforcer for admin/audit events that guarantees immutability (WORM), residency-aligned retention, and machine-readable evidence exports. This task covers: (1) policy DSL for retention + residency rules (control plane), (2) enforcement hooks that stamp/anchor events on write (storage layer), (3) an automated evidence bundler for timely exports and notarization, and (4) observability surfaces for SLOs and verification. The enforcer must support per-organization and per-region retention windows, legal-hold overrides, and signed manifests for downstream escrow. Work must consider runtime performance (latency amplification), storage cost, and compatibility with Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL: control plane exposes retention/residency policy with versioning and audit history
Write-path stamping: all admin-access and config-change events are immutably stamped (hash + timestamp + signer) at write time
WORM enforcement: backend storage enforces append-only semantics or returns an error if an attempted mutation violates retention policy
Notarized export: evidence bundler can produce a time-bounded export manifest (signed by HSM or KMS) including cryptographic anchors
Region-aware: enforcement respects per-org residency settings; exported bundles include residency metadata
Observability: dashboards for stalled exports, retention overruns, failed stamping with alerting runbook
Performance: median admin-event write latency regression < 10% at p50 and p95 under baseline workload
End-to-end test: e2e smoke verifying WORM behavior, legal-hold override, and manifest verification via test HSM
notes: 2025-02-10 — Ticket created by Aisha to centralize several audit-related runbooks; initial spike indicated two viable approaches: (A) enforce immutability at object-store layer via signed retention manifests, (B) implement a sealing service that periodically anchors batches to an HSM-notarized ledger.

2025-02-14 — Architecture sync: decided to combine approaches. Use object-store write-locks for immediate WORM guarantees where supported, and fall back to sealing service with HSM anchoring for platforms without native WORM. Trade-off: slightly higher cost and complexity but broader coverage across Dedicated/Private deployments.

2025-02-20 — Design review feedback from Security (Priya Patel): require KMS key attestation and rotation plan; recommend limiting sealing-service private keys to HSM-backed KMS only. Action: add KMS attestation step and key-rotation playbook to scope.

2025-02-25 — Engineering update: implemented policy DSL prototype in the control plane (branch: feat/eng/ENG-271828-policy-dsl). PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4472 — awaiting design review for policy UI mappings.

2025-03-01 — Performance spike test: write-path stamping added 6% median latency at 5k rps synthetic; p95 hit 12% in synthetic peak; further micro-optimizations planned: async sealing and write-ahead hash so callers wait only for local commit.

2025-03-03 — PM review (Daniel Ortega): requested legal-hold semantics and an explicit 'escrow-ready' state for exported bundles with copy-of-manifest. Added acceptance criteria and export manifest fields.
2025-03-05 — Security flagged additional requirement: export manifests must include signer certificate chain and residency attestation. Marked security_review_required = true.
design_decisions: Decision: Hybrid enforcement model — prefer native WORM object-store where available, otherwise use periodic sealing service anchored to KMS/HSM
Decision: Control plane policy DSL is authoritative (single source of truth) and will be stored as immutable versions; agents read policy versions and enforce locally
Decision: Exports are generated as monotonic bundles containing compressed events, per-bundle manifest, and a signed anchor (timestamp + merkle root) for cross-verification
Trade-off: Immediate sealing on write increases latency; mitigated via local write-ahead hash and async remote anchoring to meet latency SLOs
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike): implement policy DSL prototype and sealing-service proof-of-concept — complete
Phase 2 (Core): add write-path stamping, integrate with object-store retention API and KMS signing (ETA 2 weeks)
Phase 3 (Export): build evidence bundler + notarization + export API and e2e tests (ETA 3 weeks)
Phase 4 (Rollout): Canary in staging with selected customers, monitor observability and costs, then regional rollout
risks: Risk: Increased write latency for admin-heavy workloads may impact control-plane UX — mitigation: async anchoring and rate-limited sealing batches
Risk: Cross-region exports could leak residency metadata if not carefully packaged — mitigation: include residency labels and only allow exports per-residency boundary
Risk: KMS/HSM integration increases operational complexity — mitigation: automated key-rotation runbooks and fallback modes for on-prem customers
qa_plan: Unit and integration tests for policy DSL parsing and enforcement rules
E2E test harness to simulate mutation attempts during retention windows and verify failures
Chaos test: simulate sealing-service outage and verify system preserves local write immutability and queues exports
Manual verification: run export manifest verification using test HSM and compare anchor hashes to sealing-service ledger
rollout_and_monitoring: Canary gating metric: fraction of admin events successfully stamped and signed within 2s
Alerts: failed stamping rate > 0.1% for 5m, export job backlog > 1 hour
Dashboards: retention policy drift, export backlog, sealing-service latency, KMS sign error rate
Runbook: steps to isolate failed sealing, re-run bundler, and re-anchor bundles plus customer notification template
